mcp-server-csharp-guidances.title: MCP Server C# Guidances
mcp-server-csharp-guidances.shortDescription: Best practices for writing a stateless MCP server in C# with the official v2.0 SDK.
mcp-server-csharp-guidances.description: A guidance prompt for designing and implementing an MCP server in C# that matches the official v2.0 SDK.

content.introduction: The official Model Context Protocol C# SDK reached v2.0 on July 28, 2026, with a paradigm shift: stateless protocol by default, standardized HTTP headers and multi round-trip requests. This prompt gathers the rules to hand to a coding agent so it produces a correct MCP server, deployable on serverless as well as multi-instance setups.
content.sources: Sources: MCP C# SDK v2.0 announcement on the
useCases: Expose an internal source of truth (product catalog, directory, knowledge base) to an assistant, with permissions enforced on every call.
Wrap an existing business API behind typed MCP tools instead of letting the model build HTTP calls itself.
Automate side-effecting operations (job restart, cache purge) with user confirmation through the MRTR mechanism.
Migrate an MCP server written with the v1 SDK to v2.0: remove session state and validate multi-instance deployment.
Deploy on serverless or behind a load balancer without sticky sessions, every call being self-sufficient.
Frame a code review: use this prompt as a checklist to review an existing MCP server, section by section.
Build an internal MCP server to tool up the team: prepared SQL queries, report generation, ticket access.
